I farm only 4.1 mu, and my land is in the usual wheat-maize rotation, so I will keep the full 4.1 mu in both crops across the year. Because my family has some off-farm work, I will not chase the highest possible input level. I will aim for stable yield, manageable labor, and low risk. I have farmed for 40 years and I have well irrigation, so I will rely on improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use to what is needed to avoid obvious losses. For wheat, I will use rotary tillage after maize because it is practical on my small area and fits my labor situation. I will irrigate around the overwintering recovery, jointing, and grain filling periods if moisture is short. For maize, I will sow soon after wheat harvest, keep the same 4.1 mu in maize, and use no-tillage or very light disturbance to save time and keep the season moving. I will put more nitrogen on maize than on wheat, but still keep inputs moderate because my land is small and I care more about reliable returns than heavy spending. My goal is steady grain production from both crops using the water access I already have.
